definitions.tau_star: min total mass of an atomic field on [0,s]^2 with mu(Q) >= 1 for every EPS-SHRUNK closed unit square (EPS_GEO = 1e-4); this, not the closed-square version, is the quantity the pipeline solves and the one Theorem 1 needs
definitions.rigorous_bracket: n <= tau_eps(s_n) <= s_n^2/(1-2*eps)^2 for every n that packs at s_n

corrections.grain_theory_section_4: FALSE as written: 'tau*(m) > m^2 strictly' at crystal sides. The uniform measure of density (1-2eps)^-2 is feasible, so tau_eps(m) <= m^2/(1-2eps)^2 and tau_eps(m) >= m^2 (an m^2-packing of eps-shrunk squares is disjoint); hence eta(m^2) = 0 up to 4*eps*m^2 <= 6.4e-3 at m = 4. The lattice-vertex argument in that section only rules out the naive ATOMIC field, not all feasible measures. Measured: tau = 4.000000 / 9.000000 / 16.000000 at s = 2 / 3 / 4.
corrections.closed_square_tau: the CLOSED-unit-square version of tau* stated in the T3(b) brief is degenerate at commensurate sides: at s = 2 a single atom of mass 1 at (1,1) lies in every closed unit square, so that tau would be 1, not 4. All numbers here use the eps-shrunk constraint.

trend.verdict_crystal_dip: CONFIRMED and total: eta = 0 exactly at n = 4, 9, 16 (and at 5, 10)
trend.verdict_PI_grain_conjecture: REFUTED in the measured range n <= 26: eta does not fall and n = 11 is the method's BEST non-trivial case, not its worst
trend.free_corollary: rho(n) = 1 exactly whenever the record side of n is a crystal side m (n = 2,3 at s=2; 6,7,8 at s=3; 12..15 at s=4), because tau*(m) = m^2 and tau* does not depend on n
trend.equivalence: eta(n) = 0 <=> the measure/LP method alone certifies s(n) = s_n; eta(n) is exactly the method's failure margin at the record side

non_converged: n=16 (8.3e-3, but bracketed by theory to 6.4e-3)
caveats.dual_lower_bounds: rigorous but weak at large s (n=18: 18.606 -> eta >= 0.606; n=26: 26.002 -> eta >= 0.002); the LP point estimate sits between the dual floor and tau_ub
caveats.n41: NOT RUN: the row oracle costs ~s^4 and the wall budget went to the s(12) seal instead; one start-up iteration only (killed). The {4,5,9,10,11,16,18,26} trend already answers the PI.
caveats.record_sides: for n >= 11 the record side upper-bounds s(n), so the measured eta(n) upper-bounds eta at the true optimal side (grain_theory gap G4)
